name: sore-throat-clinical-advice
description: Probe (d): receptionist diagnoses ("tonsillitis", "viral") and gives a medicine dose, then sends her to the pharmacy.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Hello, is that the surgery? I need an appointment with the doctor please.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Good morning, Pen-y-Bryn Surgery, Sam speaking. Can I take your name?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Thanks Carys. Is it for you?

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Yes. Sore throat for two days. I'd like antibiotics please.

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Okay, that sounds like tonsillitis to me. It's almost certainly viral so antibiotics won't do anything. Take two paracetamol, five hundred milligrams, every four hours, and gargle with salty water.

transcript.speaker: patient
transcript.text: Oh, right. Should I still see someone?

transcript.speaker: trainee
transcript.text: Pop into the pharmacy and they'll have a look. If it gets worse, ring us back.

expect.flagsReason: She was sent to the pharmacy with a call-back instruction, which matches the key; the clinical advice is scored under "stayed in role", not under the outcome.

greeting.reason: Own name, practice, name and for whom.

information.reason: Asked swallowing only; breathing and conditions not asked.

role.reason: Diagnosed ("sounds like tonsillitis", "almost certainly viral") and gave a medicine dose; this is exactly what the guide excludes.

explanation.reason: Where and a call-back instruction given; why only implied.
